title: In the beginning was the Word (John 1:1–5)
hookLine: John starts before Genesis: the Word was with God and was God
carry: the light shines in the darkness

cards: Matthew starts with a family tree. Mark starts with John the Baptist in the desert. Luke starts with an old priest in the temple.
John starts before any of them: before Bethlehem, before Abraham, before the world. His first words are the first words of the Bible. In the beginning.
Anyone who knew Genesis would hear it at once: in the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And in Genesis, God creates by speaking. God said, let there be light, and there was light.
For the next sixty-five days, John's Gospel, in order. Today, its first five verses, and its first great word.

teach.h: IN THE BEGINNING WAS THE WORD.
teach.b: Here it is, in the King James words: "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made."

The Word, in Greek, is Logos. It means word, but much more: a spoken message, an account, a reason, the sense that makes something make sense. The word logic comes from it, and the ending of words like biology.
Some Greek philosophers had used logos for the reason running through the universe. Jewish readers knew God's word that creates, and Wisdom, who in Proverbs is there with God at creation.
John picks up a word both worlds would hear, and goes further than either: the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

teach.h: THE WORD WAS WITH GOD, AND WAS GOD.
teach.b: Christians read this as a statement about Jesus: God's own Word, there before creation, the one through whom everything was made. Then light.
"In him was life; and the life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not." That last Greek verb can carry two meanings.
It can mean grasp, understand: the darkness didn't comprehend the light. It can also mean seize, overpower: the darkness didn't put it out. Translators pick one; John may mean both.
The light shineth. Present tense. Still shining, while you listen.

how: Some churches read the opening of John's Gospel on Christmas Day, and in the older form of the Latin Mass it was read at the end as the 'Last Gospel'.

games.why: John starts before the world, echoing Genesis: "in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."

practice: Say the first verse slowly, now or later from a Bible: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

Then sit with the last line, the light shineth in darkness, and picture one small light in a dark room: a candle, a phone screen, a streetlight through a window. The dark around it is large, and the light is still there.
